text: I grew up working in the fields.
I know how to plant, harvest, and irrigate, but I don't enjoy it.
I often leave tasks unfinished and get scolded for it.
My father says I don't focus enough.
My mother says I need discipline.
Senaka tells stories that feel more interesting than work.
Chapala sometimes talks about hidden places in the palace-monument complex.
I think he might be right about some things.
The temple chants feel strange but important.
I do not understand the Song, but I remember parts of it.
I once followed Tarala into parts of the forest I was not supposed to enter.
We found old stone markings on the ground.
They did not look like farm structures.
I did not tell my parents.
The Agnikanda is something adults avoid explaining clearly.
Different people describe it differently.
That confuses me.
Sometimes I feel like I was born after something important already happened.
I do not know what that 'something' is.
I sometimes feel like the settlement is holding its breath.
Marisha says food is safety.
Bhumaka says work is survival.
Senaka says stories are memory.
I don't know which one is true.
I think they might all be missing something.
